source: THE OWNER'S OWN MESHY SESSION, 2026-08-02 (board SG-87) - not generated by tools/meshy.py, so there is no prompt, no task id and no credit line. It REPLACES this pipeline's own generated drone, whose record is kept below under `superseded`.
stated_role: AMBIGUOUS - 'Sentry Sphere' names two different things in this game: the GUNNER (a hovering propeller drone enemy) and the player's SENTRY skill (which draws an element-tinted ballista billboard).
role_verified_by: RENDERED AND COMPARED AGAINST BOTH, the hulk-mapping rule (SG-76: verify by looking, not by reading the file name). Against assets/art/enemies/drone_front_idle.png it matches item for item - riveted brass disc body; ONE round glowing pale-blue lens with a cross-spoke window in the centre of the face; three two-blade propellers in ring mounts, one on top and one to each side; two chains hanging beneath with pointed iron weights; a small pod under the hull. Against assets/art/props/harpoon_ballista.png (what the sentry skill draws) it shares NOTHING: the ballista is a ground-mounted crossbow on a timber base with horizontal bow arms and a bolt, and this model has no bow, no bolt, no base and no ground contact at all. The part-segmentation file corroborates the read independently: 11 geometries, of which two pairs of 99-unit-thin plates flank the hull and one more caps the mast - four blades and a top rotor - and two 5,688-unit vertical strands hang below the body, which are the chains. Evidence at .shots/probe/.
which_file_ships: BOTH, and each for what only it can do. The TEXTURED export is the geometry that ships - it is the one with UVs and the four maps, and the drone's identity is texture (brass, the blue lens). The PART-SEGMENTATION export ships nothing: it has no UVs, no images, 517,022 triangles and flat categorical label colours, so as a model it is a fifty-times-over-budget harlequin. As DATA it is the only thing that knows which triangles are blades, which the textured file welded away. tools/split_rotors.py transfers the labels onto the textured mesh and throws the segmentation away.
shrunk_by: tools/meshy.py shrink_glb - the same re-encode every generated prop went through, four 2048 maps down to the sides the screen-height law asks for. Geometry untouched: the delivered triangle count IS the shipped one.
tri_budget_note: 10,344 against the 7,000 tools/meshy.py sets as this one asset's override, and deliberately. That override exists because a propeller blade is a thin flat plate and a decimator welds its front face to its back - the reason the pipeline's own drone came back from 3,000 with a hole punched through a blade. This model has three propellers and was never decimated; paying 3,344 triangles to keep six blades intact is the same trade the override was written to make.

superseded.prompt: A small steampunk airship drone: a riveted brass disc-shaped body with one round glowing pale blue lens in the centre of its face; four short arms, one on top and one to each side and one below, each ending in a two-blade brass propeller in a ring mount; two short chains hanging underneath with pointed iron weights. One flying machine alone, hovering level, facing forward, symmetrical. No legs, no feet, no base, no stand, no ground plane, no scenery, no duplicate, no text. Stylised game-ready steampunk airship character: blackened steel, riveted brass fittings, oxblood leather, oxidised copper accents, honest wear at the edges. Chunky readable forms and broad flat colour areas, not photoreal, no micro-detail. Flat albedo, no baked lighting, no baked shadow.
superseded.texture_prompt: Polished brass shell with blackened steel banding, a cool pale blue glass lens, verdigris in the recesses, dark iron chains and weights. Hand-painted stylised game texture: blackened gunmetal, warm polished brass, deep oxblood leather, dull oxidised-copper patina settled in the recesses, bare worn metal along the working edges. Any furnace, grate, vent, ember or lamp flame is hot orange; nothing else emits light. Broad flat colour areas, no baked lighting, no baked shadow, no text, no logos.
